description: Factor evaluation sufficiency framework. Defines the evidence dimensions required to judge factor quality. This is a spec/schema — not yet implemented as a scorecard.
disclaimer: This framework evaluates research evidence sufficiency. It does not produce trading signals, recommend factors for live use, or claim alpha.

dimensions.name: computation_integrity
dimensions.description: Is the factor correctly registered, computed, and available for all canonical symbols/timestamps?

dimensions.name: predictive_ranking
dimensions.description: Does the factor have stable, statistically significant RankIC across time?
dimensions.current_gap: n_obs per month not prominently displayed

dimensions.name: portfolio_extraction
dimensions.description: Can the factor produce usable top-bottom long-short returns with acceptable risk?

dimensions.name: quantile_shape
dimensions.description: Are bucket returns monotonic? Is signal in tails or uniformly distributed?
dimensions.current_gap: Quantile shape analysis exists in old evaluator outputs but not in new diagnostics summary. Not displayed on factor-evaluation page.

dimensions.name: direction_economic
dimensions.description: Is the factor's expected direction clear, and does the economic explanation match the formula?

dimensions.name: novelty_redundancy
dimensions.description: Is the factor distinct from existing factors? Is redundancy sufficiently measured?
dimensions.current_gap: Only 6 pairs computed out of C(71,2)=2485 possible pairs. Most factors show NO_CURRENT_PAIR. Within-family redundancy (e.g., mom_5h/10h/20h/40h/72h) not systematically measured.

dimensions.name: extensibility
dimensions.description: Can new factors be added through a documented pipeline and automatically receive all evaluations?
required_evidence: All scripts in pipeline are deterministic
Page builder consumes all new outputs
dimensions.current_gap: Pipeline works but regeneration contract is not documented as a single authoritative reference.

rankic_vs_sharpe_explanation.description: RankIC and Sharpe measure different evidence dimensions and are not expected to always agree.

rankic.question: Does the factor correctly rank assets by future return?
rankic.strengths: Robust to outliers, direction-free, works with non-normal distributions
rankic.weaknesses: Does not account for portfolio construction, transaction costs, or return magnitude

sharpe.question: Does a long-short portfolio based on the factor produce attractive risk-adjusted returns?
sharpe.weaknesses: Sensitive to portfolio construction choices, transaction costs, and time period

rankic_vs_sharpe_explanation.when_they_disagree: A factor can have strong RankIC (good at ranking) but weak Sharpe (poor portfolio extraction) if: (1) the signal is concentrated in tails only, (2) returns are driven by a few months, (3) the factor is direction-ambiguous. This is NOT a simple contradiction — it requires investigation within the evidence framework.
rankic_vs_sharpe_explanation.recommendation: Use RankIC for initial screening, Sharpe for portfolio viability. Investigate disagreements using quantile shape, monthly stability, and cumulative curve evidence.
